generated_state_first_findings.global_caveat: State-first reading treats watermelon.sh as the audited primary surface. Other Watermelon-named domains, repositories, marketplace pages, and third-party references are related-surface pressure only until ownership or entity continuity is reviewed.

coherencia.title: The owned story is coherent, but the entity boundary is not
coherencia.finding: watermelon.sh presents a clear owned story around design infrastructure for modern startups and a founder pain point: startups move quickly while design becomes a bottleneck. That is a coherent primary-surface claim. The problem is not the claim itself; it is that the wider evidence set also contains Watermelon-named developer, repository, marketplace, alternatives, and adjacent-domain surfaces whose relationship to watermelon.sh is not verified.
coherencia.confidence: medium for owned-surface observation, low for cross-surface entity interpretation
coherencia.uncertainty: Do not merge the adjacent surfaces into one entity or roadmap without human review.

coherencia.title: The code-review/copilot signal should be held outside the core narrative for now
coherencia.finding: The baseline treats an open-source code-review/copilot surface as part of the Watermelon story. State-first generation keeps that signal separate: it may be relevant to a broader ecosystem, but the current evidence does not prove it is an official extension of the design-infrastructure surface.
coherencia.uncertainty: Repository ownership, naming variance, and relation to watermelon.sh require review.

diferenciacion.title: Differentiation currently rests on an owned platform claim
diferenciacion.finding: Watermelon differentiates itself through the language of infrastructure, ecosystem, and relief from fragmented design tools. That is a stronger and more specific claim than a generic design-service offer, but the available evidence supports it as owned positioning rather than externally validated differentiation.
diferenciacion.confidence: medium for claim visibility, low for market validation
diferenciacion.uncertainty: No external proof in the current set validates whether the infrastructure claim is recognized by users or the market.

diferenciacion.title: The strongest safe reading is problem framing, not strategic intent
diferenciacion.finding: The brand's safest differentiating signal is its problem frame: founders stitching tools together, inconsistent UI, and design slowing product development. The report can say this is the brand's chosen frame. It should not infer a full platform strategy, category ownership, or adoption pathway from that copy alone.
diferenciacion.uncertainty: External corroboration is needed before treating the problem frame as market truth.

percepcion.title: Perception is fragmented by evidence collection, not necessarily by the market
percepcion.finding: The evidence set exposes several Watermelon associations: the primary design-infrastructure surface, GitHub repositories, a Product Hunt listing, alternatives pages, and unrelated-looking news coverage. State-first reading does not frame this as proven public confusion. It frames it as an evidence-ecology problem: Brand3 cannot yet tell which surfaces belong to the same entity.
percepcion.confidence: medium for evidence fragmentation, low for audience-perception claims
percepcion.uncertainty: Audience perception should not be inferred from search/evidence collision alone.

percepcion.title: Product Hunt is a visibility signal, not traction proof
percepcion.finding: The Product Hunt profile can support the observation that a Watermelon product surface exists in an early-adopter channel. It cannot support a claim about adoption, feedback quality, or traction without engagement data and entity review.
percepcion.uncertainty: Use only as a related visibility signal unless ownership and current relevance are verified.

presencia.title: The primary owned presence is small but legible
presencia.finding: watermelon.sh gives Brand3 a usable primary surface: a focused domain, a clear startup/design-infrastructure line, and basic crawl/indexing files. The safer presence finding is that the owned footprint is narrow but legible, not that the brand has an SEO or acquisition problem.
presencia.uncertainty: A small sitemap can indicate focus, early stage, or incomplete indexing; the current evidence does not decide among them.

presencia.title: Developer surfaces widen presence but also raise review burden
presencia.finding: GitHub surfaces add technical presence, but they also increase ambiguity. The report should show them as possible related developer surfaces, not as confirmed proof that the design-infrastructure brand has an active open-source community.
presencia.uncertainty: Entity relation and official status are unresolved.

vitalidad.title: Vitality signals are present but not entity-safe
vitalidad.finding: The baseline uses watermelon.us for founding, hiring growth, and funding signals. State-first reading holds those claims as potentially useful but not entity-safe for watermelon.sh. They should not be used to describe the audited brand's vitality until the relationship between surfaces is verified.
vitalidad.uncertainty: Funding, employee growth, and founding claims may belong to a different Watermelon entity.

vitalidad.title: External activity is mixed and partly irrelevant
vitalidad.finding: The alternatives page, repository activity, and unrelated-looking produce/news reference do not form one clean vitality signal. The safer reading is that external collection is noisy: some surfaces may indicate low developer or marketplace activity, while others should be excluded or reviewed before interpretation.
vitalidad.uncertainty: Do not aggregate these as one vitality score narrative without entity filtering.

specificity.reason: The new findings name the actual composition problem instead of repeating generic strategy choices.

evidence_binding.reason: Each generated finding states what the evidence can and cannot support.

entity_coherence.reason: The entity ambiguity is centralized as the governing condition for the report.

caveat_discipline.reason: Repeated no-external-corroboration caveats are replaced by one global caveat and local uncertainty boundaries.

narrative_cohesion.reason: Dimensions coordinate around a shared entity problem instead of treating each finding as a separate paragraph task.

uncertainty_preservation.reason: Uncertainty is more explicit and less repetitive; however, it still dominates the case because the evidence is genuinely ambiguous.

overreach_risk.reason: The new findings avoid unified roadmap, adoption, market traction, and intent claims.

brand3_floc_voice.reason: The writing is more direct, bounded, and evidence-aware, though still more diagnostic than editorial.

what_failed: The trial still required manual generation; it does not prove an automated generator can do this.
The evidence set is so entity-ambiguous that the better narrative remains heavily bounded.
Generated findings are clearer but not yet production-ready report copy.
A shared evidence map must exist before generation; otherwise the model will reintroduce surface merging.
verdict.biggest_improvement: The state-first version turns fragmented findings into one coordinated entity-composition reading.
verdict.biggest_remaining_risk: False coherence could return immediately if related surfaces are treated as aliases or official proof.
